risks: Minimal: reading existing records on hospital premises; the main risk is privacy and the identification of individual anaesthetists' practice.
consent: Individual consent is impracticable for 546 past patients; the research ethics board will be asked for a waiver of consent for secondary use under minimal risk.
data: Extraction on hospital premises into a study database with study numbers; anaesthetists are coded and never reported individually; the key is held by the health records department.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: patients who needed an interpreter or whose risk factors were not recorded may have lower recorded risk scores and less prophylaxis; interpreter use and missing history are recorded and adherence is reported by them. Sex is part of the risk score and is reported.
effectiveness: The study is useful if it shows whether adherence support should be the unit's next improvement target.
efficiency: About 55 hours of fellow time; no new data collection.
costs: Fellow time within training allowances; no other costs.
partnerships: Recovery nurses (case definition and the log), the day surgery patient panel (plain-language summary), and the anaesthesia department's education lead.
rebPath: Application to the research ethics board for secondary use of records with a waiver of consent, following ICH-GCP and the Declaration of Helsinki; not yet submitted, so no extraction starts before the decision. Records access is already approved (HR-2026-118).
limitations: Residual confounding by indication; incomplete case capture at busy times; single unit.
summary: Minimal-risk record study awaiting an ethics decision on a consent waiver; anaesthetists never identified.
